words.en: to go wrong; a problem arises
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as chū wèntí. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 系统出问题了. Hindari: 出问题 is too vague for escalation — add the symptom and the impact.
words.when: Remember 出问题 like the word you’ll use when a work process isn’t running as it should — open the status, then name where the problem sits.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 出问题 as a workplace status opener for systems, logins, or processes that broke. Follow with the location or step (登录的时候…). Alone it is too general for a serious escalate; add symptoms and impact.

example.pinyin: Dēnglù de shíhòu chū wèntí le.
example.en: There was a problem when logging into the system.

words.en: not enough time; too late to finish
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as láibují. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 来不及准备. Hindari: 来不及 is about time; 不能 is more general inability.
words.when: Remember 来不及 like the word you’ll use when the clock, not your skill, is the blocker — you cannot finish today and need a new slot.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 来不及 when time is short for finishing or preparing something. Pair with a concrete ask (明天早上可以吗？). Do not swap it for 不能 when the issue is ability rather than the clock.

example.zh: 今天来不及做完，明天早上可以吗？
example.pinyin: Jīntiān láibují zuò wán, míngtiān zǎoshang kěyǐ ma?
example.en: There isn’t enough time to finish today — is tomorrow morning okay?

words.en: to get it wrong; to mix up
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as gǎocuò. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 搞错时间. Hindari: 搞错 is not only a technical fault — it can also mean misunderstanding information.
words.when: Remember 搞错 like the spoken word you’ll use when you grabbed the wrong fact, person, or time — admit it, then state the correction.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use informal 搞错 for mix-ups of facts, people, or schedule (搞错时间). Own the mistake and immediately give the right detail. It covers misunderstanding as well as a wrong click.

example.zh: 我搞错时间了，会议是三点。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎocuò shíjiān le, huìyì shì sān diǎn.
example.en: I got the time wrong — the meeting is at three.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as nònghǎo. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 已经弄好了. Hindari: 弄好 sounds informal; for a formal report, 完成 is cleaner.
words.when: Remember 弄好 like the practical spoken line you’ll use when a form or result is ready for someone else to use.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use spoken 弄好 when the work product is ready to hand off (已经弄好了). It is informal office talk; prefer 完成 in polished written updates.

example.zh: 表格我已经弄好了，你可以看了。
example.pinyin: Biǎogé wǒ yǐjīng nònghǎo le, nǐ kěyǐ kàn le.
example.en: I’ve finished the form — you can look at it now.

words.en: to help; to lend a hand
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as bāngmáng. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 帮个忙. Hindari: do not say 帮忙 alone without naming the help you need.
words.when: Remember 帮忙 like the short ask you’ll use when you hit a blocker and need a colleague’s contribution on a concrete check.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers request 帮忙 / 帮个忙 with a specific action (看一下这个问题). Bare 帮忙 without the ask sounds incomplete in workplace chat.

example.zh: 你能帮我看一下这个问题吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ kàn yíxià zhège wèntí ma?
example.en: Can you help me take a look at this problem?

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as jiějué. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 解决问题. Hindari: 解决 is stronger than 处理 — do not claim it is solved if you are still testing the fix.
words.when: Remember 解决 like the word you’ll use when a workplace problem has been handled to a practical root, or when you push to get a real solution.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 解决问题 for closing an issue, not just touching it. 处理 can mean “handling”; 解决 claims a solution. Wait until the fix is verified before saying it is 解决了.

example.zh: 我们先把这个问题解决。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān bǎ zhège wèntí jiějué.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as yǐngxiǎng. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 影响进度. Hindari: 影响 does not automatically mean a bad impact — state the direction if needed.
words.when: Remember 影响 like the word you’ll use when a change or problem will alter tomorrow’s schedule or another concrete work outcome.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 影响 for concrete knock-on effects (影响进度, 影响安排). Name what is affected. It can be neutral or negative — clarify severity when it matters.

example.zh: 这个变化会影响明天的安排。
example.pinyin: Zhège biànhuà huì yǐngxiǎng míngtiān de ānpái.
example.en: This change will affect tomorrow’s schedule.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as dānxīn. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 担心时间不够. Hindari: after 担心, name what you worry about — not only a vague anxious feeling.
words.when: Remember 担心 like the word you’ll use when you flag a risk at work without blaming someone — name the concrete concern.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers follow 担心 with the risk (担心时间不够). It softens escalation: you are sharing a concern, not accusing. Vague 我很担心 without an object is weak in meetings.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dānxīn jīntiān shíjiān bú gòu.
example.en: I’m worried there isn’t enough time today.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as bù qīngchu. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 还不清楚. Hindari: 不清楚 is not total 不知道 — you may know part of it while details stay unclear.
words.when: Remember 不清楚 like the honest reply you’ll use when workplace details are still fuzzy — then say how or when you will check.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 还不清楚 when status is incomplete, often followed by 我去问一下. It is softer and more precise than claiming you know nothing (不知道).

example.zh: 这个情况我还不清楚，我去问一下。
example.pinyin: Zhège qíngkuàng wǒ hái bù qīngchu, wǒ qù wèn yíxià.
example.en: This situation still isn’t clear to me — I’ll go ask.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as kǎzhù. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 系统卡住了. Hindari: for stuck interpersonal situations you can use 卡住 metaphorically, but spell out the context.
words.when: Remember 卡住 like the natural spoken word you’ll use when a system or process stops at one point — then say what you cannot do because of it.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 卡住 for a freeze or jam (系统卡住了), then name the blocked action (没法提交). It can extend metaphorically to people or workflows if context is clear.

example.zh: 系统卡住了，我现在没法提交。
example.pinyin: Xìtǒng kǎzhù le, wǒ xiànzài méi fǎ tíjiāo.
example.en: The system is stuck, so I can’t submit right now.

notes.title: Module aim — name the block, ask, then next step
notes.body: Modul 09 / Harian (book pages 30–32): explain the obstacle specifically, ask for help, then close with the next step. Indonesian title in the book: Masalah dan bantuan.

notes.title: 出问题 needs symptom and impact
notes.body: The book treats 出问题 as a status opener when something is not running as it should, with pairing 系统出问题了. Hindari: alone it is too vague for escalation — add where it fails and what it blocks.

example.pinyin: Dēnglù de shíhòu chū wèntí le.
example.en: There was a problem when logging into the system.

notes.title: 来不及 vs 不能; 解决 vs 处理
notes.body: 来不及 is about insufficient time (来不及准备), not general inability (不能). 解决 (解决问题) claims a real fix and is stronger than 处理 — do not say it is solved while you are still testing.

example.zh: 今天来不及做完，明天早上可以吗？
example.pinyin: Jīntiān láibují zuò wán, míngtiān zǎoshang kěyǐ ma?
example.en: There isn’t enough time to finish today — is tomorrow morning okay?

notes.title: Honest status: 不清楚 / 卡住 / 担心
notes.body: 不清楚 (还不清楚) means details are still unclear — often followed by checking — and is not the same as total 不知道. 卡住 names a stall point (系统卡住了). 担心 flags a risk with a concrete object (担心时间不够), without blaming a person.

example.zh: 这个情况我还不清楚，我去问一下。
example.pinyin: Zhège qíngkuàng wǒ hái bù qīngchu, wǒ qù wèn yíxià.
example.en: This situation still isn’t clear to me — I’ll go ask.

notes.title: Latihan 90 detik (book exercise)
notes.body: Book drill on p.32: pick three entries from this module — 出问题, 帮忙, and 不清楚 — and build one work or daily story that uses all three. Record without reading the PDF, then check whether your timing and decisions came out clearly. No model Chinese dialogue is printed for this drill; do not invent one as book text.

example.zh: 出问题 / 帮忙 / 不清楚
example.en: Target trio for the 90-second practice (instruction only; no sample story in the book).
